body_long:
Cheval Blanc Courchevel, the first Maison of LVMH's hotel collection, opens its winter season in December with a larger estate: two private chalets join the original Maison. The man in charge is Mathieu Hellec, General Manager since 1 October 2024.

## A career built on islands

Hellec's path is unusual for a ski palace. According to the LVMH Hotel Management announcement published in October 2024, his international experience was built mainly in Mauritius, with Constance Hotels, and in the Seychelles, at Maia, where he was director of operations. In 2021, after two years as the resort's second-in-command, he took the helm of Maia Luxury Resort and led its integration into Anantara. In 2023 he became General Manager of Kisawa Sanctuary, on Benguerra Island in Mozambique. Eric Boonstoppel, Vice President Operations of LVMH Hotel Management, welcomed him to Courchevel.

## The Maison

Cheval Blanc Courchevel has opened each winter since 2006, from December to April, in Courchevel 1850, ski-in and ski-out on Les Trois Vallées. It counts just 36 rooms and suites, including The Apartment, a 650 sqm residence with its own lift and ski room, and a team of 180 Ambassadeurs, as the house calls its staff. Its table is Le 1947, Yannick Alléno's three-Michelin-star restaurant, alongside Le Grill Alpin, La Terrasse, the bar and a smoking yurt. The spa offers Guerlain treatments, and the art collection includes works by Paola Pivi, Walter Niedermayr and Xavier Veilhan.

## Two chalets this December

As reported by A&E Magazine on 19 October 2026, two private chalets open in December 2026 opposite the Maison in the Jardin Alpin. One has five bedrooms over 900 square metres, the other nine bedrooms over 1,500 square metres; together they form a 2,400-square-metre retreat. Peter Marino designed the communal spaces, Vik Muniz painted the landscape frescoes, and a dedicated team of 15 majordomes and a private culinary team will look after guests.

## The signal

Alpine palaces are recruiting from remote island resorts. Running a lodge on a private island and a chalet at 1,850 metres demand the same craft: complete privacy, a very small number of guests, and service with no second chances. As Cheval Blanc moves from 36 keys to private houses with their own staff, that experience becomes the job description.
summary: General Manager of Cheval Blanc Courchevel since October 2024, Mathieu Hellec came from Kisawa Sanctuary in Mozambique and Maia in the Seychelles. This December he adds two private chalets to the 36-key Maison.
title: Mathieu Hellec, from island lodges to Cheval Blanc Courchevel
